title.narrative: Ukraine: Restoring Dignity and Justice in Ukraine: A Whole-of-Society Approach to Accountability for International Crimes (Phase II)

description.narrative: 1) To improve the capacities of Ukrainian criminal justice actors handling war crimes and crimes against humanity to apply adequate investigative, analytical and prosecutorial standards and methodologies. 2) to advance accountability-centred organizational reform priorities at the Office of the Prosecutor General (OPG). 3) To improve practical and theoretical knowledge of national legal actors on international humanitarian law. 4) To support Ukrainian policy makers and legal actors in increasing their capacity in implementing and understanding Transitional Justice (TJ) mechanisms and processes. 5) To strengthen cooperation on international criminal law matters through increasing awareness and implementation of mutual legal assistance and universal jurisdiction. 6) To advance TJ by providing support for addressing the roles of veterans – as victims, witnesses, perpetrators, former prisoners of war – and alleged collaborators within the criminal justice chain. 7) To strengthen the role for civil society organizations and survivor movements and victims in international accountability efforts, leading to greater transparency, documentation of war crimes, and improved access to justice for victims. 8) To enhance engagement of institutional and civil society actors in the oversight and implementation or rehabilitative, right-based practices in the treatment of conflict-related detainees.
Direct beneficiaries: The Office of the Prosecutor General, the National Police of Ukraine.Indirect beneficiaries: Justice seekers, particularly survivors and child victims of international crimes.
The project aims to advance a whole-of-society approach to accountability for international crimes in Ukraine.
